title: ECMP hash uses chained 32-bit hash_i32, not the splitmix64 named by GDD M3 canon
evidence: sim_core.gd:304: `var h := WorldSeed.hash_i32(WorldSeed.hash_i32(WorldSeed.hash_i32(WorldSeed.hash_i32(0x9E3779B9 ^ src) ^ dst) ^ ci) ^ pkt_id)` / GDD M3: "deterministic ECMP hash `splitmix64(src, dst, class, pkt_id) mod N` across equal-cost next hops"
detail: E2.1 inherits PP-Odin rulings; GDD M3 names splitmix64 over (src,dst,class,pkt_id). Implementation hashes the same tuple with a 32-bit splitmix-family chain. Deterministic, flow-pinned intent fully preserved; only the named primitive differs.
recommended_fix: Either swap _pick_next_pipe to a 64-bit splitmix64 finalizer over the same tuple, or note the owned 32-bit variant as a deliberate local substitution in SimCore's doctrine block.

title: _ready computes wedge_layout/node_placements twice despite the 'computed ONCE and threaded through' guarantee claimed by _generate_world's docstring
evidence: main.gd:38-40: `_generate_world(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED))` then `sim.setup(SEED, WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED)))`; main.gd:140-142: "The layout is computed ONCE by the caller and threaded through, so staged nodes and sim placements can never drift onto different layouts."
detail: A1's replay contract rests on staged nodes and sim placements sharing one layout. The code derives them from two independent (identical-by-purity) computations; the structural threading the comment advertises is not what runs.
recommended_fix: In _ready, compute `var layout := WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED)` once and pass it to both _generate_world(layout) and sim.setup(SEED, WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, layout)).
